From: dev_patel@redwood.com
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-18T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC - intermittent 503s when calling Redwood API

Quick head-up from runtime: we've seen a spike in requests that triggered the fallback router to a compatibility variant (compat-v1) which currently does a strict model-variant compatibility check. When the variant doesn't match the runtime constraints we return a 503 instead of queueing. Two immediate observations:

1) The POC request pattern is high-concurrency short requests (many separate websocket connections) which pushes the policy into the fallback path.
2) The compatibility check code path rejects requests where kv-cache layout differs slightly between quantized variants (we added a conservative check in Q1). That strictness is too brittle for mixed-variant traffic.

Hotfix proposal (fast):
- Relax the strict kv-cache layout check for compat-v1 (toggle behind feature-flag).
- Increase fallback queue capacity for small dedicated pools by 50% to avoid outright 503s during short spikes.

I'll open JIRA-RT-7892 with logs (attached). ETA for hotfix deployment to canary (us-west-2) ~ 3 hours if we prioritize.

— Dev
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime
attachments: logs-20260618.zip

- 12:30 PT: full route to dedicated-small for LogiMed (temporary) if metrics stable.

Please confirm that Sales/SE can inform the LogiMed demo lead of the plan & expected customer-visible effect (we expect 503s to drop to <1%). I'll prepare a short mitigation_plan.md and link the JIRA.
